newsitem.title: UK: DLR UP IN QUIET EUROPE, DEALERS PONDER DIRECTION.
newsitem.headline: DLR UP IN QUIET EUROPE, DEALERS PONDER DIRECTION.

text.p: The dollar was a touch firmer in early European trade on Thursday, reviving against the mark after Wednesday's three-pfennig tumble as market expectations of higher German interest rates intensified.

Dealers said trade was quiet amid a dearth of fresh factors. While longer-term sentiment on the dollar remains positive, traders are pondering whether it will have to lose more ground before accelerating higher again.
"There is a small rebound this morning but the market is leaning a bit more towards the downside in the short term," said Paul Meggyesi, senior analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"Residual position adjustment could continue through the rest of this week and as such the risk is that the mark continues to recover," said Meggyesi.

The mark rose across the board on Wednesday - reaching its highest level against the dollar in almost two weeks - after the Bundesbank said German inflation had picked up and that it would steer policy to ensure price stability was maintained.
The Bundesbank's comments were seen as a signal that it might be preparing the ground for higher interest rates.
At 0830 GMT the dollar was at 1.8410/20 marks, up from 1.8355/60 in late European trading on Wednesday.
Against the yen, the dollar stood at 116.15/25, up from 115.65/75.
US July CPI data at 1230 GMT are expected to show a rise of 0.2 percent on the month and 2.4 percent from a year ago.
US July instrial production data at 1315 GMT is seen rising 0.2 percent, while capacity utilisation, at the same time, is expected to show an unchanged reading of 83.5 percent.

"We doubt that any of today's numbers have the potential to impact the market significantly," analysts at Chase said in a note to clients. "The outlook for a stronger, but still not inflationary, third quarter is unlikely to be altered."

Dollar/yen pushed higher overnight amid short-covering, with stop-loss buying triggered near 115.90, traders said. The dollar faces resistance though at 116.45, a 50 percent retracement of Friday's four-yen fall.
The mark/yen cross was in the spotlight again, rising to session highs of 63.33/35 in morning European trade in a rebound from two-year lows just above 62 on Monday.

The Indonesian rupiah's tumble to historic lows against the dollar at 2,765 after the central bank abolished its intervention band dominated overnight trade. In morning Europe, it stood at 2760.00/2770.00.
The Indonesian central bank said it would stop publishing formal intervention bands for the currency.

While the move had been anticipated by many in the market, the timing came as a surprise after the Indonesian authorities on Wednesday raised interest rates and intervened to stop the rupiah breaching the bottom of the now defunct band.
"Indonesia is the latest country in the Asian region to bow to the speculative tide and abandon its currency regime for a more freely floating one," said Meggyesi.
Sterling gained ground against the mark on short-covering after Wednesday's sell-off and on the back of a firmer dollar/mark.
It was at 2.9075/85 marks from 2.9008/90818 late on Wednesday. Against the dollar it was at $1.5835/45 from $1.5841/46.

The Australian dollar was weaker after unexpected weakness in wages data left the door open for another cut in interest rates, dealers said. It stood at US$0.7430/35, compared with US$ 0.7453/58 at the Sydney close on Wednesday.
-- Astrid Zweynert London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
